examples.ko: 그는 돌부리에 걸려 넘어져서 무릎을 다쳤어요.
examples.en: He tripped on a jagged stone and hurt his knee.
There are lots of jagged stones on the road, so walk carefully.

examples.ko: 아이가 화가 나서 돌부리를 힘껏 걷어찼어요.
examples.en: The child got angry and kicked a stone as hard as he could.

examples.ko: 산길을 걷다가 돌부리 때문에 발목을 삐었어요.
examples.en: While walking on the mountain path, I sprained my ankle because of a stone.
I kicked a stone and my shoe came off.
I dug out the protruding stones from the field one by one.

explain: '돌멩이'는 돌 하나를 가리키지만, '돌부리'는 땅에 박혀 위로 튀어나온 돌의 끝부분을 말해요. 보통 '돌부리에 걸리다', '돌부리에 채이다'처럼 걷다가 발이 걸리는 상황에서 말해요.

phrases.en: I almost tripped on a stone on the dark road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 걷다가 발이 돌에 걸리는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for a foot catching on a stone.

phrases.en: I kicked a protruding stone on the mountain path, and my foot hurt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 튀어나온 돌을 발로 차거나 부딪히는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Has a stronger feeling of kicking or bumping into a protruding stone.
phrases.en_equiv: to stub one's foot on a stone

phrases.en: The path is rough, so watch out for the stones.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길을 걷는 사람에게 조심하라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to warn someone walking on a rough path.

explain_en: '돌멩이' means a single stone, but '돌부리' is the tip of a stone stuck in the ground and sticking up. It is usually used in situations like '돌부리에 걸리다' or '돌부리에 채이다', where your foot catches on it as you walk.

examples.en: A heavy frost fell overnight and the cabbages froze.
The heavy autumn frost ruined the pepper crop.

examples.ko: 된서리가 내리기 전에 고구마를 캐야 해요.
examples.en: We have to dig up the sweet potatoes before the heavy frost comes.
I'm worried because the heavy frost came early this year.

examples.ko: 아침에 밭에 나가 보니 된서리로 하얗게 덮여 있었어요.
examples.en: When I went out to the field in the morning, it was covered white with heavy frost.

examples.ko: 갑자기 불어닥친 불황에 가게들이 된서리를 맞았어요.
examples.en: Shops were hit hard by the sudden downturn.

explain: 늦가을에 농작물이 상할 만큼 아주 세게 내리는 서리예요. 일상에서는 '된서리를 맞다'라는 비유로 더 자주 들을 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 새로 낸 가게가 갑작스러운 불경기로 된서리를 맞았어요.
phrases.en: The newly opened shop was hit hard by the sudden recession.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 크게 타격을 받거나 큰 피해를 입을 때 써요. 주로 일, 사업, 계획에 나쁜 일이 닥쳤을 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone or something suddenly takes a heavy blow or suffers great damage. It is mostly said when something bad hits work, business or plans.

explain_en: It is a very heavy frost in late autumn, strong enough to damage crops. In daily life you are more likely to hear it in the figurative expression '된서리를 맞다'.

examples.ko: 창문을 열어 두었더니 비가 방 안까지 들이쳤어요.
examples.en: I left the window open, and the rain blew right into the room.

examples.ko: 비가 들이치니까 창문 좀 닫아 주세요.
examples.en: The rain is blowing in, so please close the window.

examples.ko: 바람이 세서 눈이 베란다까지 들이치고 있어요.
examples.en: The wind is strong, so snow is blowing in even onto the balcony.

examples.ko: 이 집은 창이 커서 햇빛이 깊숙이 들이쳐요.
examples.en: This house has big windows, so sunlight pours deep inside.

examples.ko: 소나기가 갑자기 들이쳐서 옷이 다 젖었어요.
examples.en: A shower suddenly blew in and my clothes got soaked.

examples.ko: 파도가 갑판 위로 들이치자 모두 소리를 질렀어요.
examples.en: When a wave crashed onto the deck, everyone screamed.

explain: 일상에서는 비·눈·바람·햇빛이 안쪽으로 세게 뿌려 들어올 때 써요. '비가 들이치다'가 대표적인 짝이고, 그냥 '들어오다'보다 세찬 느낌이 있어요. 창가나 베란다 이야기를 할 때 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The window is open, so the wind and rain blow in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비와 바람이 함께 세게 안으로 들어올 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for rain and wind blowing in hard together.

phrases.en: Every morning sunlight pours into my room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 햇빛이 안쪽까지 환하게 들어올 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used when sunlight shines brightly far into a room.

phrases.en: I went inside to avoid the rain blowing in.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'으로 뒤의 명사를 꾸며서 안으로 몰아치는 비를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-는' form describes rain that blows in from the side.

explain_en: In daily life it describes rain, snow, wind or sunlight blowing or streaming forcefully inward. '비가 들이치다' is the classic pairing, and it feels stronger than a plain '들어오다'. It often comes up when talking about windows and balconies.

examples.en: Two seed leaves came out of the seed.
The bean I planted in the pot has opened its seed leaves.
The seed leaves come out before the true leaves.
A new leaf is rising from between the seed leaves.

examples.ko: 아이들이 관찰 일지에 떡잎 모양을 그렸어요.
examples.en: The children drew the shape of the seed leaves in their observation journal.

examples.ko: 이 식물은 떡잎이 하트 모양이라 귀여워요.
examples.en: This plant's seed leaves are heart-shaped, so it's cute.

explain: 씨앗에서 싹이 틀 때 가장 먼저 나오는 잎이에요. 나중에 나오는 '본잎'과 구별해서 쓰고, 과학 수업이나 식물 키우기 이야기에 자주 나와요. '떡잎부터 알아본다'라는 속담으로도 많이 알려져 있어요.

phrases.example: 저 아이는 어릴 때부터 달랐어요. 될성부른 나무는 떡잎부터 알아본다더니.
phrases.en: That child was different from early on. They say you can tell a promising tree from its seed leaves.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크게 될 사람은 어릴 때부터 남다른 모습이 보인다는 뜻의 속담이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb meaning that someone who will do great things already shows signs of it when young.
phrases.en_equiv: Talent shows from an early age.

explain_en: It is the first leaf that comes out when a seed sprouts. It is distinguished from the later '본잎' (true leaf) and often appears in science classes and talk about growing plants. It is also well known through the proverb '떡잎부터 알아본다'.

examples.en: The ship stopped in the middle of the boundless sea.
Looking out at the endless ocean made my heart feel refreshed.

examples.ko: 혼자 유학을 와서 망망대해에 던져진 기분이었어요.
examples.en: Coming to study abroad alone, I felt as if I had been thrown into a vast ocean.
I watched the ship heading out to the open sea for a long time.
Preparing for a job felt like an endless ocean, and I was lost.
I heard the sound of waves from the open sea all night.

explain: 끝이 보이지 않을 만큼 넓은 바다를 말하고, 일상 대화보다는 글이나 뉴스에서 많이 보여요. 앞이 막막한 상황을 비유해서 '망망대해에 던져진 기분'처럼도 써요.

phrases.en: A small boat is sailing across the open sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끝없이 넓은 바다를 배로 나아간다는 뜻으로 글에서 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means sailing a ship across an endless sea, often seen in writing.

phrases.example: 혼자 외국에 오니 망망대해 같은 느낌이에요.
phrases.en: Coming abroad alone, I feel like I'm adrift in an endless sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞이 막막한 기분을 비유할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a metaphor for feeling lost with no clear way ahead.
phrases.en_equiv: to feel like an endless sea

phrases.example: 창문 너머로 끝없이 넓은 바다가 보여요.
phrases.en: Through the window I can see the endless wide sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: '망망대해'를 일상 대화에서 쉽게 풀어 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy way to say '망망대해' in everyday conversation.

explain_en: It means a sea so wide that no end is in sight, and it appears more in writing and news than in daily talk. It is also used as a metaphor for feeling lost, as in '망망대해에 던져진 기분'.

examples.ko: 학교 앞길에 벚나무가 쭉 심어져 있어요.
examples.en: Cherry trees are planted all along the road in front of the school.

examples.ko: 봄이 되면 벚나무에 꽃이 활짝 펴요.
examples.en: When spring comes, the cherry trees bloom fully.
The street trees in my neighborhood are cherry trees.
We ate a packed lunch with my family under a cherry tree.
The cherry tree leaves have already turned red.

examples.ko: 이 벚나무는 나이가 백 년이 넘었대요.
examples.en: I heard this cherry tree is over a hundred years old.

explain: 꽃은 '벚꽃', 나무는 '벚나무'로 나눠 말해요. 봄에 꽃을 보러 가는 것은 '벚꽃 구경'이나 '벚꽃놀이'라고 해요. 소리는 [번나무]로 나요.

phrases.en: When the cherry blossoms bloom, the park is crowded.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나무가 '벚나무'라면 그 꽃은 '벚꽃'이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The tree is 벚나무, and its flower is 벚꽃.

phrases.en: I walked slowly along the cherry tree path by the river.
phrases.nuance_ko: 벚나무가 줄지어 서 있는 길을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A road lined with cherry trees.

phrases.en: I'm going to see the cherry blossoms this weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 봄에 꽃을 보러 가는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Going out to enjoy the blossoms in spring.

explain_en: The blossom is '벚꽃' and the tree is '벚나무'. Going to see the blossoms in spring is called '벚꽃 구경' or '벚꽃놀이'. It is pronounced [번나무].

examples.en: The snowy scenery of Seoraksan is truly beautiful.

examples.ko: 창밖의 설경을 보며 따뜻한 차를 마셨어요.
examples.en: I drank warm tea while looking at the snowy view outside the window.

examples.ko: 눈이 와서 온 마을이 설경으로 변했어요.
examples.en: It snowed, and the whole village turned into a snowy scene.
I climbed the mountain to take photos of the snowy landscape.

examples.ko: 겨울에는 설경을 보러 오는 관광객이 많아요.
examples.en: In winter, many tourists come to see the snowy scenery.

examples.ko: 설경이 멋진 곳으로 여행 가고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to travel somewhere with beautiful snowy scenery.

explain: 눈이 덮인 풍경을 감상하듯 말할 때 쓰는 말이에요. 여행 소개나 사진 설명에서 자주 보이고, 일상 대화에서는 '눈 온 풍경'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I enjoyed the snowy view from the mountaintop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈 덮인 풍경을 천천히 바라본다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It feels like slowly looking at a snow-covered scene.

phrases.en: Jeju Island in winter has a beautiful snowscape.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장소의 눈 풍경을 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to praise a place's snowy scenery.

phrases.en: I sent my friend a photo of the snowy scene.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈 덮인 풍경을 찍은 사진을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for a photo of a snow-covered landscape.

explain_en: It is used when admiring a landscape covered in snow. It often shows up in travel guides and photo captions, and in daily talk people also say '눈 온 풍경'.

examples.en: The car got stuck in the mire and couldn't move.
After the rain, the road turned into a mire.
I want to escape from the quagmire of debt.
Once you fall into a quagmire, it's hard to get out.
The economy is sinking into a quagmire.

examples.ko: 이 늪은 수렁 같아서 발이 푹 빠져요.
examples.en: This swamp is like a bog, and your feet sink right in.

explain: 진흙이 깊어 발이 빠지는 곳이지만, 실제로는 빚, 불황, 절망처럼 헤어나기 힘든 상황을 비유할 때 더 자주 들려요. '늪'과 비슷하게 쓰는데 '수렁'은 빠져나오기 힘들다는 느낌이 강해요.

phrases.en: The company sank into a long recession.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제 진흙이 아니라, 빠져나오기 힘든 나쁜 상황에 놓였다는 비유예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Not real mud: it figuratively means being stuck in a bad situation that is hard to escape.

explain_en: It is literally deep mud that swallows your feet, but it is often heard as a metaphor for situations that are hard to escape, such as debt, recession or despair. It is close to '늪' (swamp), with a strong sense of being unable to get out.

examples.ko: 옛날부터 금실 좋은 부부를 원앙에 빗댔어요.
examples.en: Since long ago, a loving married couple has been compared to mandarin ducks.

examples.ko: 호숫가에서 원앙 한 쌍이 헤엄치고 있어요.
examples.en: A pair of mandarin ducks is swimming by the lake.

examples.ko: 저 부부는 원앙처럼 늘 붙어 다녀요.
examples.en: That couple is always together, like lovebirds.
Male mandarin ducks have colorful feathers.

examples.ko: 결혼 선물로 원앙 모양 장식품을 받았어요.
examples.en: I got a mandarin duck ornament as a wedding gift.
A mandarin duck, a natural monument, was spotted near here.

explain: 실제 새 이름이기도 하지만, 한국에서는 금실 좋은 부부를 떠올리게 하는 새예요. 그래서 결혼 선물이나 혼례 장식에 자주 나와요. '원앙새'라고도 해요.

phrases.example: 두 분은 원앙 같은 부부로 소문났어요.
phrases.en: The two of them are known as a loving couple.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사이가 아주 좋은 부부를 칭찬할 때 써요. 새 이야기가 아니라 부부 사이를 비유하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise a couple who get along very well. It is a comparison about the marriage, not about birds.

explain_en: It is the name of an actual bird, but in Korea it also brings to mind a loving married couple. So it often shows up in wedding gifts and decorations. It is also called '원앙새'.

en: to wrap; to cover; to blanket

examples.en: I wrapped the baby in a blanket and ran to the hospital.
Thick fog enveloped the whole village.
The flames spread, engulfing the building in an instant.

examples.ko: 분노가 그의 마음을 휩싸 버려서 아무 말도 못 했어요.
examples.en: Anger took over his mind, so he couldn't say anything.

examples.ko: 깨지기 쉬운 컵은 신문지로 휩싸 두세요.
examples.en: Wrap fragile cups in newspaper.
It felt as if sadness was wrapping around my whole body.

explain: 감정이나 소문에 '휩싸이다'는 아주 자주 쓰지만, 능동형 '휩싸다'는 불, 안개, 감정처럼 덮는 쪽이 주어일 때나 천으로 둘러 쌀 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 물건을 감쌀 때 '싸다', '감싸다'를 더 많이 써요.

phrases.en: The building was engulfed in flames in an instant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불, 안개, 감정 등에 완전히 덮일 때 쓰고 '휩싸다'보다 훨씬 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when fully covered by fire, fog, or emotion; much more common than 휩싸다.

phrases.en: The mother wrapped the baby in a blanket.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이나 사람을 둘러 싸는 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An everyday word for wrapping around an object or person.

phrases.example: 짙은 어둠이 온 마을을 휩싸고 있어요.
phrases.en: Deep darkness is covering the whole village.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 있다'를 붙여 지금 덮고 있는 상태를 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-고 있다' describes something that is covering right now.

explain_en: The passive '휩싸이다' (as in being caught up in emotions or rumors) is very common, whereas the active '휩싸다' is used when the subject is what covers, like fire, fog or emotion, or when wrapping something in cloth. In daily talk, '싸다' and '감싸다' are more common for wrapping objects.

examples.en: I suffered heartache for a long time because of unrequited love.

examples.ko: 이별 후 가슴앓이로 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: After the breakup I could not sleep from heartache.
After much inner anguish, I opened up to my friend.
Don't suffer alone in your heart. Try telling someone.

examples.ko: 그 노래는 가슴앓이하는 사람들에게 위로가 돼요.
examples.en: That song comforts people who are nursing heartache.
My heartache is so bad that it is hard even to eat.

explain: 마음속으로 혼자 속을 태우며 힘들어하는 것을 말해요. '가슴앓이를 하다'가 대표적인 짝말이고, 짝사랑이나 말 못 할 고민에 자주 써요. 문맥에 따라 속이 쓰린 증상(속쓰림)을 뜻하기도 해요.

phrases.en: Don't suffer alone, try telling someone.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가슴앓이를 하다'를 붙여 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A contracted form of 'gaseumari-reul hada'.

phrases.en: I couldn't say it and just suffered inside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말 못 하고 속으로만 힘들어할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you suffer inwardly without speaking.

phrases.en: I went through a lot of emotional hardship.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래 마음이 힘든 것을 넓게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broader word for long emotional hardship.

explain_en: It refers to suffering quietly and alone inside, worrying and aching. The typical pairing is '가슴앓이를 하다', often used for unrequited love or worries you cannot talk about. Depending on context it can also mean heartburn as a physical symptom.

en: to be disagreeable; to be unpleasant; to be feeling bad

examples.ko: 제 말을 고깝게 듣지 말아 주세요.
examples.en: Please don't take what I said the wrong way.
My friend's joke bothers me a little.
I was upset back then, but I understand it all now.

examples.ko: 그렇게 말하면 상대가 고깝다고 느낄 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you say it that way, the other person may feel offended.

examples.ko: 말없이 떠난 게 고까워서 연락을 안 했어요.
examples.en: I was annoyed that he left without a word, so I didn't contact him.

examples.ko: 고까운 마음이 들어도 먼저 이야기해 보세요.
examples.en: Even if you feel resentful, try talking about it first.

explain: '서운하다'보다 상대 말이나 행동이 나를 무시하거나 비꼬는 것처럼 느껴져 언짢은 느낌이 강해요. '고깝게 듣다', '고깝게 들리다'로 가장 많이 써요. ㅂ 불규칙이라 '고까워요', '고까운', '고까웠어요'가 돼요.

phrases.en: That remark sounded a bit offensive to me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고깝게 듣다'는 내가 그렇게 받아들이는 것이고, '고깝게 들리다'는 말이 저절로 그렇게 느껴지는 거예요.
phrases.nuance_en: 고깝게 듣다 is how I take it; 고깝게 들리다 is how it naturally comes across.

phrases.en: Please don't speak in such a snide tone.
phrases.nuance_ko: ㅂ 불규칙 활용형 '고까운'으로 명사 앞에서 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: The irregular form 고까운 modifies a noun that follows.

phrases.en: That remark doesn't bother me at all.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기분이 상하지 않았다고 말할 때 쓰는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used to say you were not offended.

explain_en: Compared with '서운하다', it carries a stronger sense of being annoyed because someone's words or actions felt dismissive or sarcastic. It is most often used as '고깝게 듣다' or '고깝게 들리다'. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so it becomes '고까워요', '고까운' and '고까웠어요'.

examples.ko: 그는 큰 결정을 앞두고 깊은 고뇌에 빠졌어요.
examples.en: Facing a big decision, he fell into deep anguish.
The main character's anguish was felt throughout the movie.

examples.ko: 오랜 고뇌 끝에 회사를 그만두기로 했어요.
examples.en: After long agonizing, I decided to quit my job.
The author put human anguish into the novel.
I could see traces of anguish in his expression.
Everyone has the anguish of making choices.

explain: '걱정'이나 '고민'보다 훨씬 무겁고 깊게 괴로워하는 말이에요. 일상 대화의 '고민'과 달리 소설, 영화 평, 연설에서 자주 나와요. '고뇌에 빠지다', '고뇌에 찬 얼굴'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 그는 선택을 앞두고 오랫동안 고뇌에 빠져 있었어요.
phrases.en: He was lost in anguish for a long time before making his choice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 괴로운 생각에서 벗어나지 못하는 모습을 말하는 가장 흔한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the most common expression for being stuck in painful thoughts.

phrases.example: 고뇌에 찬 얼굴로 편지를 읽고 있었어요.
phrases.en: He was reading the letter with an anguished face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표정에서 깊은 괴로움이 보일 때 쓰며, 글이나 영화 묘사에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when deep suffering shows on someone's face, often in written or film descriptions.

phrases.example: 요즘 진로 고민이 많아서 잠을 못 자요.
phrases.en: I have a lot of worries about my career path these days, so I can't sleep.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고뇌'보다 가볍고 일상적이에요. 대화에서는 보통 '고민'을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is lighter and more everyday than 고뇌, and in conversation 고민 is the usual choice.

explain_en: It describes much heavier and deeper suffering than '걱정' or '고민'. Unlike everyday '고민', it often appears in novels, film reviews, and speeches. It is used as in '고뇌에 빠지다' and '고뇌에 찬 얼굴'.

en: to anguish; to be in agony

examples.en: He agonized for a long time over his career path.

examples.ko: 주인공은 선택 앞에서 고뇌하는 모습을 보여 줘요.
examples.en: The protagonist shows himself agonizing over a choice.

examples.ko: 혼자 고뇌하지 말고 친구와 이야기해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't agonize alone; talk with a friend.

examples.ko: 철학자들은 삶의 의미를 두고 고뇌해 왔어요.
examples.en: Philosophers have agonized over the meaning of life.
After agonizing all night, I finally wrote the letter.
We need time to grow while struggling through anguish.

explain: '고민하다'를 더 무겁고 진지하게 말하는 표현이에요. 일상에서는 '고민하다'가 자연스럽고, '고뇌하다'는 글, 인물 묘사, 연설에 어울려요. '깊이 고뇌하다'처럼 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 그는 깊이 고뇌한 끝에 결정을 내렸어요.
phrases.en: After agonizing deeply, he made his decision.
phrases.nuance_ko: '깊이'와 함께 쓰면 오랫동안 크게 괴로워했다는 느낌이 더 분명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 깊이, it more clearly conveys suffering greatly over a long time.

phrases.example: 주인공이 고뇌하는 모습이 영화에서 인상 깊었어요.
phrases.en: The way the main character agonized was impressive in the movie.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인물이 괴로워하는 모습을 그릴 때 쓰는 말로, 글이나 영화 이야기에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when describing a character's suffering, and fits writing and film talk.

phrases.en: I'm trying to decide what to eat for lunch.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고뇌하다'보다 가볍고 일상적이라서 대화에서 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is lighter and more everyday than 고뇌하다, so it sounds more natural in conversation.

explain_en: It is a heavier, more serious way of saying '고민하다'. In daily life '고민하다' is natural, while '고뇌하다' fits writing, character descriptions, and speeches. It is often used as '깊이 고뇌하다'.

examples.ko: 이 가게가 문을 열기까지는 많은 곡절이 있었어요.
examples.en: There were many twists and turns before this shop opened.
After many twists and turns, he came back to his hometown.

examples.ko: 친구는 저에게 곡절을 묻지 않고 도와줬어요.
examples.en: My friend helped me without asking for the whole story.
There were hard times too, but I'm happy now.

examples.ko: 그 곡절을 다 설명하려면 하루가 걸려요.
examples.en: It would take a whole day to explain all the circumstances.

examples.ko: 어떤 곡절로 그 일을 맡게 됐어요?
examples.en: Under what circumstances did you end up taking that job?

explain: 일이 복잡하게 얽힌 사정이나 사연을 말해요. 보통 '곡절이 많다', '곡절이 있다'로 쓰고, '우여곡절'이라는 말로 더 많이 들어요. '이유'보다 사연이 길고 굴곡이 있다는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: After many twists and turns, we got married.
phrases.nuance_ko: '곡절'보다 더 자주 쓰는 말로 여러 번 겪은 어려움과 변화를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: More common than '곡절', it refers to many ups and downs.

phrases.en: That family has a lot of complicated history.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사연이 복잡하고 많을 때 쓰는 기본 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic pairing for when there is a complicated, long story.

phrases.en: This song has a sad story behind it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 뜻이지만 더 부드럽고 일상에서도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning but softer and used in daily talk too.

explain_en: It means the complicated circumstances or story behind something. It is usually used as '곡절이 많다' or '곡절이 있다', and you hear it more often in the word '우여곡절'. Compared with '이유' (reason), it suggests a longer story with twists.
